{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian Cuisine]]

'''Onion chutney''' is a delicious sweet-and-sour chutney used as a side dish for many South Indian snacks and breakfast items. It is one of the components used in ''masala dosa'' assembly.

== Ingredients ==

*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chickpea|channa]] [[Cookbook:Dal|dhal]]
*2 medium-sized red [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], coarsely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*3 pieces of [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]], each 1x1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Tamarind|tamarind]] paste
*4–6 dried red [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==

# In a shallow pan, heat the oil. Add the chana dal, and stir until the dal is roasted.
# Add the onions, and [[Cookbook:Stir-frying|stir fry]] them till they become transparent and the edges turn golden brown. Turn off the heat and let them cool for a few minutes.
# When cooled, blend together the onion mixture, coconut, chillies, tamarind, and salt until it makes a smooth paste. Add a few teaspoons of water if necessary.
